sources.citation: Guy, J.B.M. 1972. A grammar of the northern dialect of Sakao, a Melanesian language of Espiritu Santo (New Hebrides). PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl 1885/130469 (published in revised form as Pacific Linguistics B-33, 1974).
sources.note: SAKAO (saka1289), not Nethalp: word-level ('secondary') stress falls on the final syllable of each word, retracting to the penult when the final syllable's vowel is the high central vowel; phrase-level ('primary') stress falls on the last such word-final syllable before the phrase-final intonation contour or on the phrase's last syllable; monosyllabic particles usually unstressed; stress = loudness + vowel length. Same rule as Guy 1974 PL B-33 and Guy 1977 JPS.

sources.note: No synchronic statement of where stress falls in Lorediakarkar. The only prosody-relevant content is diachronic: loss of *ŋ conditioned by 'post-tonic environments' in earlier stages of Shark Bay and Lorediakarkar (i.e. Guy assumes a historically innovated word stress whose position conditioned segment loss, as in his 1978 Shark Bay account: stress innovated usually on the penult, later 'no longer emic'). p.19-20 notes the Tryon 1976 lists are not phonemicised; p.28 says Shark Bay and Lorediakarkar have 'extraordinary phonologies' inadequately reflected in the lists.
